1:1.devotion: John opens his short letter as an elder writing to a local congregation pictured as a mother and her children. He anchors the greeting in love grounded in truth—a love shared not only by him but by everyone who has come to know the truth of Christ.
1:1.reflection: Is my love for other believers grounded in shared truth, or only in shared preferences and comforts?
1:1.action: Reach out to a fellow believer today whom you know only loosely, and express genuine encouragement in Christ.
1:1.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for uniting Your people in truth. Widen my circle of love beyond those easiest to love, and help me cherish every believer because we share Your truth together. Amen.

1:2.devotion: John explains why his love endures: the truth itself dwells in him and his readers and will remain with them forever. Christian fellowship is not built on fleeting circumstances but on God's unchanging truth, which lives within believers and binds them together across time and distance.
1:2.reflection: When circumstances shift, do I lean on God's unchanging truth or on unstable feelings?
1:2.action: Memorize one short verse about God's truth today and repeat it whenever anxiety or doubt surfaces this week.
1:2.prayer: Father, thank You that Your truth is not a passing idea but a living presence that abides in me and will remain forever. Anchor my heart in what cannot change or fade. Amen.

1:3.devotion: John greets his readers with a blessing of grace, mercy, and peace flowing from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. These gifts come marked by truth and love—the twin themes of the letter—reminding believers that God's favor is both real and relational.
1:3.reflection: Do I receive God's grace, mercy, and peace as daily gifts, or do I try to earn what He freely gives?
1:3.action: Begin your day tomorrow by consciously thanking God for grace, mercy, and peace before checking your phone or starting any task.
1:3.prayer: Gracious Father, thank You for grace, mercy, and peace given through Your Son. Help me live today from these gifts rather than striving for them, walking in both truth and love. Amen.

1:4.devotion: John shares his deep joy at discovering some of the lady's children walking in truth, just as the Father commanded. For John, obedience is not a burden but a walk—a steady way of living. Nothing delights a spiritual father more than seeing faith carried into daily conduct.
1:4.reflection: Whose faith has brightened because they watched me walk in truth?
1:4.action: Tell someone today, perhaps a parent or mentor, about a believer whose faithful walk has encouraged you recently.
1:4.prayer: Father, make my daily walk honest and true, not just my words. Let my life bring joy to those who have guided me in faith and honor to You who commanded the truth. Amen.

1:5.devotion: John pleads with the congregation to love one another—not a new commandment, but the one given from the beginning of their faith. The oldest instruction is still the most urgent. Truth matters deeply to John, yet love remains the command that ties it all together.
1:5.reflection: Is there a believer I have drifted from loving, even while holding firm to right doctrine?
1:5.action: Take a concrete step of reconciliation today—send a message, make a call, or offer an apology to someone within the church family.
1:5.prayer: Lord, You commanded love from the beginning, and I still need the reminder. Soften my heart toward the people in my church family, and let love mark me as much as conviction. Amen.

1:6.devotion: John defines love practically: walking according to God's commandments. Love is not merely warm feeling but obedient daily living, the same walk heard from the beginning. Truth and love converge here—loving God and others is shown in steady, faithful steps, not slogans.
1:6.reflection: How does my love show up in actual obedience this week, not just in good intentions?
1:6.action: Choose one command of Christ you have known but postponed obeying, and take a first obedient step today.
1:6.prayer: Father, turn my love from feeling into walking. Show me one concrete act of obedience today that expresses love to You and to my neighbor, and give me grace to follow through. Amen.

1:7.devotion: John warns that many deceivers have gone into the world, refusing to confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh. In John's day, some denied that Jesus truly became human. He names such teaching deceiver work and antichrist spirit, urging believers to hold firmly to the real incarnation of Christ.
1:7.reflection: Do I know Christ as He truly is, or am I tempted to reshape Him into a version that suits me?
1:7.action: Spend ten minutes today reading a Gospel passage about Jesus' real, human life, and thank God that the Son truly came in the flesh.
1:7.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for truly becoming human—living, suffering, and rising for us. Guard me from distorted teachings, and keep my faith anchored in who You really are. Amen.

1:8.devotion: John urges his readers to watch over their own spiritual lives. The apostles and teachers had labored among them, and John wants their work to stand. Perseverance matters: staying faithful to Christ's teaching means the reward received at the end will be full, not diminished.
1:8.reflection: Am I actively watching over my own walk with Christ, or have I grown spiritually careless?
1:8.action: Set aside ten minutes today to honestly review how you have cared for your faith this past week.
1:8.prayer: Lord, keep me attentive to my soul. Guard what has been built in my life through faithful teaching, and help me persevere so that my reward in You is full. Amen.

1:9.devotion: John draws a clear line: remaining in the teaching of Christ—about who He is and what He commanded—is the mark of truly knowing God. Wandering beyond it, in this letter's context, meant denying core truth about Jesus. Abiding in Christ's doctrine means abiding in fellowship with Father and Son.
1:9.reflection: Is my confidence rooted in the actual teaching of Christ, or in ideas I find more comfortable?
1:9.action: Read one Gospel passage today and note one thing Jesus actually taught that you can obey this week.
1:9.prayer: Father, keep me anchored in Your Son's teaching. When new voices compete for my attention, help me test everything by Christ and remain in fellowship with You. Amen.

1:10.devotion: John writes to a congregation facing traveling teachers who denied essential truth about Christ. He instructs the church not to extend hospitality that would endorse their ministry. This concerns official welcome of false teachers, not ordinary kindness to unbelievers, whom we are called to love.
1:10.reflection: Do I discern carefully which teachers I endorse, without becoming harsh toward people still learning?
1:10.action: Before sharing or recommending a sermon, book, or teacher this week, briefly check its message against Scripture.
1:10.prayer: Lord, give me discernment to recognize teaching that distorts Your Son, and grace to speak truth lovingly while still showing kindness to every person I meet. Amen.

1:11.devotion: John explains the previous warning: greeting and supporting such teachers made one a participant in their work. Endorsement carries weight. In the ancient world, welcoming a traveling teacher signaled public approval of his mission. John wants the church's support reserved for the truth.
1:11.reflection: When I lend my approval to something, do I realize others may follow my example?
1:11.action: Identify one platform or influence you have, and today use it deliberately to encourage sound, Christ-centered teaching.
1:11.prayer: Father, remind me that my words and welcome influence others. Keep my encouragement aligned with Your truth, so that everything I support points people toward Your Son. Amen.

1:12.devotion: John has more to say but prefers face-to-face conversation over ink and paper. Christian fellowship is embodied, not merely written. He looks forward to a personal visit, expecting that being together in person will bring joy to its fullness between him and this beloved congregation.
1:12.reflection: Which brother or sister in Christ needs my actual presence, not just a message?
1:12.action: Arrange an in-person visit, call, or shared meal this week with a fellow believer you usually only text.
1:12.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the joy of embodied fellowship. Help me value presence over convenience, and let my time with other believers be rich, honest, and full of joy. Amen.

1:13.devotion: John closes with greetings from the members of a sister congregation—the children of an 'elect sister' church. This brief note reminds readers that the early church was a connected family. Congregations cared for one another, prayed for one another, and passed on warm greetings across distance.
1:13.reflection: Do I remember that I belong to a worldwide family of believers, not just my local church?
1:13.action: Send a greeting today to a believer or congregation in another place, letting them know you remember them in prayer.
1:13.prayer: Father, thank You for uniting Your people across cities, nations, and generations. Teach me to love the whole family of God, remembering distant brothers and sisters with genuine care. Amen.
